newsitem.title: FINLAND: VALMET "NO RICHER OR POORER" ON PORSCHE.
newsitem.headline: VALMET "NO RICHER OR POORER" ON PORSCHE.

text.p: Valmet Automotive, the car-making arm of Finnish engineering group Valmet Oy, is expecting a neutral impact on group earnings from an assembly deal announced with German sportscar maker Porsche on Friday.
"Our operations do not make Valmet much richer, but not much poorer either," Juhani Riutta, President and CEO of Valmet's Automotive unit told Reuters by telephone.
The Automotive unit accounted for about four percent of Valmet's January-August net sales at 7.36 billion markka.
Valmet's eight-month profit after financial items was 664 million markka and Automotive's earnings were "positive".
Valmet Automotive and Porsche AG earlier on Friday announced an agreement for Valmet to build more than 5,000 Porsche Boxster cars per year at its Uusikaupunki plant.
The number of Porsche cars to be assembled in Finland is likely to be far higher than annual the minimum of 5,000 announced in a letter of intent, Riutta said.
"The figure 5,000 is a minimum," he said. "But it all depends on the markets."
Riutta said the start of Porsche production will need "significant new" investments at Uusikaupunki, but these would be financed by the Automotive unit itself.
The number of Automotive employees is expected to increase by about 200 due to the deal from 1,145 at end-August, he said.
Riutta said the Porsche deal would serve as an important reference and strengthen Valmet Automotive's profile as a specialty car manufacturer.
"Everyone is interested in good references and there could not be a better reference than Porsche," he said.
